clue.text: Heartlessly allow bird to suffer — animal!

indicators.note: to suffer is to be knocked about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
without a heart: the middle letter of the five-letter word allow is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its central L
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone lets a bird come to harm, and the exclamation condemns them as a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' takes the middle L from ALLOW, leaving ALOW; add BIRD and 'to suffer' rearranges ALOWBIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild boar is a species of wild pig, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Accept wife's appreciation of music

parts.note: having an ear for music means appreciating it

explanation.surface: A man accepts that his wife understands music well.
explanation.walkthrough: To wear something, in the informal British sense, is to tolerate or go along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to wear a proposal is to put up with or tolerate it.

clue.text: Writer of letter US prosecutor dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the prosecutor's letters are removed

parts.note: lambda is the Greek letter L
a DA is a District Attorney, the US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A writer of a letter is dropped by an American prosecutor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'letter' is the Greek one, not a piece of correspondence; Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was an English essayist, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Ordered a book about criminal

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: told, as in told to do something, means ordered

explanation.surface: Someone orders a book about crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it turns TOLD A B round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad lot is an informal name for a dishonest or disreputable person, a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Fighting here in North Wales

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Loggerheads is a village in North Wales

explanation.walkthrough: Loggerheads is a real village in Denbighshire, North Wales; the second definition reads the phrase literally as a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in strong disagreement with someone is the idiomatic sense of the phrase; the place name gives a literal reading.

clue.text: Divine-like poem one's written during last month

indicators.note: written during puts the poem inside the month

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated DEC
If is Kipling's famous poem
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A godly poem composed late in the year, in December.
explanation.walkthrough: IF is Rudyard Kipling's well-known poem, a stock crossword reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Deific means godlike or making divine, so it is an adjective for something divine in nature.

clue.text: That is upsetting about BBC boss — untouchable but showing nerves

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed letters go around the boss
upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, i.e. backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the head of the BBC is the Director-General, DG
Eliot Ness led the US agents nicknamed The Untouchables

explanation.surface: Upsetting news about the BBC's chief, someone untouchable, now seems to be anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC's head is its Director-General; 'untouchable' recalls Eliot Ness, the Prohibition agent whose team were The Untouchables.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves as a noun means anxiety or tension, the same state as edginess.

clue.text: Laminate used for worktops — police workers supply it

definitions.note: worker ants produce and spray this acid; 'it' stands for the answer

parts.note: Formica is a brand of plastic laminate for kitchen surfaces
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A laminate for kitchen worktops supplied by police employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' doubles up: with 'police' it reads as staff, but the definition means worker ants, which make the acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Formic acid is named from the Latin for ant, because ants secrete it.

clue.text: Maybe a Guardian feature about German child replaced

indicators.note: about means surrounding: the chin goes round the angel

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a guardian angel, so an angel is a kind of guardian

explanation.surface: A feature in this newspaper about a German child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper, but it is the angel. The chin is a feature of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy infant left in place of a stolen human baby.

clue.text: Being shelled, one commando unfortunately gets into difficulty

parts.note: a means one
the Royal Marines (RM) are the British commando force

indicators.note: gets into puts the word inside the other

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
ill as in ill-fated means unfortunately

explanation.surface: A soldier under shellfire, one unlucky commando, finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' suggests artillery fire, but it means having a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an animal protected by a bony armour shell, so it is a shelled creature.

clue.text: Waiting nervously for outcome, swimming not the snooker

indicators.note: swimming means moving around in a blur, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone waits anxiously for a result, watching swimming instead of snooker on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the' looks like an instruction to delete THE, but those letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on tenterhooks is an idiom for suspense, from cloth stretched taut on a frame.

clue.text: A pain in the neck about police officer

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a drag is a tedious nuisance

explanation.surface: A police officer comes about a nuisance complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garda (Garda Síochána) is the police force of Ireland, and an officer is also called a garda.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ireland a garda is a member of the national police force, a policeman or policewoman.

clue.text: Established diary has entry for November evening, Tory leader admitted

indicators.note: has entry for lets the letter in inside the diary

parts.note: a log is a daily record
N is November in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: admitted means taken inside

parts.note: evening means making level, as sanding a surface does

indicators.note: leader means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A diary entry records a November evening, with the Tory leader present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not the night time but levelling off, as with sandpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-standing has existed for a long time and is firmly established.

clue.text: Family spokesman's reckoned he'd be staying with them

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

indicators.note: a spokesman speaks the word out loud, giving its sound

parts.note: reckoned means guessed

explanation.surface: A family spokesman supposes their visitor will stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reckoned' said aloud gives a word that sounds like a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A house guest is a visitor who stays overnight or longer in someone's home.

clue.text: Granada finally supply Bieber with a TV contract

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of Granada

indicators.note: supply read as supple, bending, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Granada television signs Justin Bieber to a TV deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun (a TV deal) but is the verb meaning shorten. 'supply' is read as 'supple-y', loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate a word is to shorten it, which is one sense of contracting it.

clue.text: Eyes other blokes, discontentedly

indicators.note: without contents: only the outside letters of each word remain

parts.note: first and last letters of other
first and last letters of blokes

explanation.surface: A dissatisfied person looks enviously at other men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes' looks like a verb (ogles) but is the plural noun; orbs is a poetic word for eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs is a literary term for eyeballs, from their round shape.

clue.text: Bird with muscles kept turning round, looking primarily for bouncer

indicators.note: turning round means the whole thing is read backwards
kept means held inside, so the muscles go inside the bird

parts.note: a linnet is a small finch
abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter

parts.note: first letter of looking

explanation.surface: A muscular bird spins about, scanning for a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but it is something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis ball is designed to rebound off the court, so it is a thing that bounces.

clue.text: Relationships in trouble over independence issue

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
issue means offspring, here sons

explanation.surface: Relationships go sour over a dispute about independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic of debate, but it means children, as in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a connection or relationship, often a secret romantic affair.

clue.text: Sort out high night rates

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone must deal with expensive overnight charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like it describes the expensive rates; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten a matter is to resolve it or put it in order.

clue.text: Right to compare with deposed king?

indicators.note: deposed means removed from power, so the king's letter goes

parts.note: to liken is to compare with
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question whether one might compare one's rights with those of a toppled monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing K from LIKEN leaves the legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal claim to keep someone's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Butt of lowbrow gag — poor fellow

indicators.note: the butt is the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: last letter of lowbrow
to gag is to retch

explanation.surface: The target of a crude joke is an unfortunate man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' and 'gag' suggest the target of a joke; here they mean the end letter and to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate or pitiable person.

clue.text: Have a go and weigh it! Rival uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain suggests unsettled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A boxer is urged to try out and weigh in, though the rival's status is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a whirl is an idiom for trying it out or attempting it.

clue.text: Look at half a dozen we sent over

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then reversed

explanation.surface: Instructions to inspect six items that have been shipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To view something is to inspect it or look it over.

clue.text: Journalist over the pond taken advantage of

parts.note: across the Atlantic, i.e. American, abbreviated US
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor

explanation.surface: An American reporter has been exploited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the pond' is a British phrase for America, across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used means being exploited by someone for their own benefit.

clue.text: Divine creature in Mile End shop not revealing name

indicators.note: End means the final letter

parts.note: last letter of Mile

indicators.note: not revealing means the name is withheld, so its letter is removed

parts.note: to shop is to inform on, i.e. to rat on

explanation.surface: A godly person in a Mile End shop keeps their name secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Mile End is a district in East London; 'shop' is British slang for informing on someone, RAT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, minor goddesses of Greek myth, so she is a divine being.

clue.text: Starts panicking about money and also about drinks

indicators.note: about means surrounding: the panicking word goes round the rest

parts.note: a horse that shies starts in fright

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Someone becomes panicky about money and about the cost of drinks too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' is not a first-letters signal: a nervous horse starts, or shies. The two 'about's do different jobs, one surrounding and one turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothies are thick blended fruit drinks.

clue.text: Believer cross at robbery

parts.note: a T is cross-shaped
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A religious person angry at a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but stands for the T-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in the existence of God.

clue.text: Had nothing to do with key getting cut

parts.note: ESC is the Escape key on a keyboard
hewed means cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone avoided having a key cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately avoid or abstain from it.
